newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First says talks well advanced, much work ahead.
newsitem.headline: NZ First says talks well advanced, much work ahead.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Wednesday said talks towards forming a coalition government were well advanced but there was still an "enormous" amount of work to get through.

"We are a long way into the process. For example we have announced... our desire to have a comprehensive agreement on how a coalition would behave with respect to its constituent parties and I think we are a long way down the track on that," he said.
However, Peters also stressed "the enormous amount of work that has to be done".
He was speaking after the sixth round of talks between nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power, and the caretaker National Party government and centre-left Labour Party.
Labour leader Helen Clark reiterated she was keen for New Zealand First to express a preference for a coalition with Labour as soon as possible.
"I've always said it would be towards the end of this month before a preference was expressed," Clark said.
Both National and Labour aim to form a coalition government with NZ First support after last month's inconclusive general election.
Peters also said he had passed on a report on state house rentals, provided by the government, to Labour. NZ First and Labour have said they want to cooperate over the issue.
